ext.description: Cursor-style coding agent for VS Code powered by Hermes Agent over ACP, with your own model endpoint.
ext.untrusted: The Hermes agent is disabled until the workspace is trusted.
cfg.path: Path to the `hermes` executable. Leave empty to search `PATH` and the default install location.
cfg.language: Language of the Hermes panel. The default is Indonesian; `auto` follows the VS Code display language. Command Palette titles always follow the VS Code display language.
cmd.removeApprovalHook: Remove Terminal Approval Hook from Hermes Config
cfg.activeProfile: Active endpoint profile: `hermes` (your own Hermes config) or the id of a profile in `hermes.profiles`.
cfg.profiles: Custom endpoint profiles. API keys are stored separately in VS Code SecretStorage, never here.
cfg.mcpServers: MCP servers passed to Hermes for IDE sessions (stdio: `command` + `args`; http/sse: `url`).
cfg.askEveryCommand: Ask before every terminal command the agent runs, not only the ones Hermes considers risky. Uses a Hermes `pre_tool_call` hook that only acts when Hermes is started by the IDE.
cfg.nodePath: Node.js used to run the terminal approval hook. Empty = Node on `PATH`, then the Node bundled with Hermes.
cfg.useCtrlK: Bind Ctrl+K (when text is selected) to Hermes inline edit. Turn off to keep VS Code's Ctrl+K chords with a selection.
cfg.completionEnabled: Inline Tab suggestions from a separate FIM model (outside Hermes).
cfg.completionBaseUrl: OpenAI-compatible base URL of the FIM model, e.g. `http://localhost:11434/v1` (Ollama) or a vLLM server. The API key is kept in SecretStorage.
cfg.completionTemplate: How the fill-in-the-middle prompt is built. `auto` picks from the model name; `suffix` lets the server do it from `prompt` + `suffix`.
cfg.completionMaxTokens: Maximum tokens per multi-line suggestion (single-line suggestions use at most 48).
cfg.completionDebounce: Wait this long after typing before asking the model.
cfg.indexEnabled: Embed workspace files for semantic search (@codebase and the codebase_search tool for Hermes).
cfg.indexBaseUrl: OpenAI-compatible base URL for `/embeddings`. The API key is kept in SecretStorage.
cfg.indexMaxFileKB: Skip files larger than this when indexing.
cfg.updateCheck: Check for a new Hermes IDE release in the background (standalone IDE only). The only request is a GET for the release feed; no code or prompts are sent.
cfg.updateFeedUrl: Override the release feed URL (a `latest.json` over https). Leave empty to use the one built into the IDE.
cmd.hermesSetup: Set Up the Model with the Hermes Wizard
cfg.pricing: Prices per 1 million tokens, by model id, used to estimate cost: `{ "claude-sonnet-4-5": { "input": 3, "output": 15, "cachedInput": 0.3 } }`. A model matches by exact id, by id without its provider prefix, or by the longest entry its id ends with. Models without an entry are not costed; the IDE never guesses prices.
cfg.usageCurrency: Symbol shown before costs in the usage report, matching the currency your prices are in.
cfg.notifyMode: When to notify that the agent finished or needs a permission: `off`, `unfocused` (only while the window is in the background) or `always`.
cfg.notifyMinSeconds: Do not notify about a finished turn shorter than this many seconds. Permission requests always notify.
cfg.notifyNative: Also show a Windows notification, so it is seen when the window is hidden.
cfg.hermesUpdateCheck: Once a week, ask Hermes (`hermes update --check`) whether an update exists and tell you. Hermes contacts its own repository for this; nothing is ever installed without your confirmation.
cfg.privacyLocalOnly: Full local mode: keep code and prompts on this computer or on servers you list. The agent is blocked while its model endpoint is on the internet, Hermes' network tools (web search, web extract, browser, vision) are blocked, Tab completion and the codebase index are off for remote endpoints, remote MCP servers are not passed to Hermes, and update checks are off. Terminal commands you approve can still use the network; ones that look like it are flagged. Application-scoped: a project cannot change it.
cfg.privacyAllowedHosts: Hosts treated as yours in full local mode, such as your own server (`vps.example.com`, or `*.example.com` for subdomains). Loopback and private-network addresses are always accepted. Application-scoped.
cfg.routingEnabled: Automatic model routing: a light model for short questions, a strong one for heavy work (Plan mode, attached folders or lots of code, images, long or refactor-style requests) and a fallback model when the chosen one fails. Every switch is written in the chat with its reason; picking a model yourself pauses routing for that session. Application-scoped.
cfg.routingLight: Model for short, simple questions. Use a name from the model list (for example `qwen2.5-coder:7b`); empty keeps the selected model.
cfg.routingHeavy: Model for heavy work. Use a name from the model list; empty keeps the selected model.
cfg.routingFallback: Model to retry with once when the chosen one fails with an authentication, rate-limit, quota or server error. Empty turns the fallback off.
cfg.routingMaxChars: A message longer than this many characters counts as heavy work.
cfg.tasksMaxParallel: How many parallel agent tasks may run at once. Each is a separate Hermes process in its own git worktree, so memory and model usage grow with it.
cfg.agentLanguage: Language the agent answers in. `ui` (default) uses the panel language, `id` or `en` force one, `off` sends no language instruction. The agent still follows the user when they write in another language.
cfg.learningLevel: Depth of the explanations in learning mode: `beginner` (plain words, terms defined) or `intermediate` (reasons, alternatives and trade-offs).
cfg.deployTargets: Servers for deploying over SSH, shown in the Hermes tools card. Each has a name, host, user and optionally a port, the path of a private key file (never its content), the project folder on the server, a git remote name, and your usual deploy steps. Application-scoped: a project cannot add a server to its own settings, because a registered server changes how commands to it are labelled.
